# Native ONNX runtime evidence

The immutable reference remains Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. Reference collectors verify the unchanged GPU installer, requirements and configuration against that commit. The released GPU installer completed in disposable storage using its hash-locked binary wheels. An independent collector derives file sizes/hashes from the actual reference installations' wheel `RECORD` entries, verifies every selected file against those entries and checks official PyPI wheel metadata against the released requirements. Expected artifacts are not generated through the native installer. Collectors remain outside the maintained tree under ignored task scratch.

`released-onnx-runtime.json` has SHA-256 `5b867c38e14e6ec1ca3a1fda13b22c74110d2f8f2ad2e4cedd897b2f8112a471`. It freezes CPU ONNX Runtime 1.30.0, CUDA ONNX Runtime 1.26.0, seven released NVIDIA package pins, exact archive/member sizes and SHA-256, license notices and 40 independent GPU-storage decisions. Accepted storage cases are witnessed through the released installer's actual `uv venv` subprocess entry; only filesystem capacity measurements are substituted. Both sides preserve the 3.5 GB GPU reservation, 5 GB combined local budget, 6 GB temporary free-space requirement and exact boundary messages.

The native installer downloads those wheels as archives and extracts only allowlisted native libraries and notices. It creates no Python environment and installs no interpreter, Python package code, binding extension or headers. CPU has four members totaling 29,338,945 bytes; CUDA has 34 members, including 25 libraries and nine notices, totaling 3,247,698,857 bytes. Completion markers depend on pinned native assets, not a Python ABI. CPU native files also count toward the combined storage budget. The compiled `ort` API 26 bindings load the selected library explicitly; they never download or upgrade a runtime themselves.

Four ordinary tests cover pinned artifacts/storage witnesses, real loopback archive downloads, selective extraction, declared sizes, whole/member hashes, missing files, unsafe paths, duplicate destinations, cache reuse, private file permissions, retained old runtimes on failure, post-promotion staging/backup recovery and real storage ownership. A deliberately included Python canary member is never installed. The completion-marker permission check failed before the native repair and passes with mode 0600. These selective-extraction and replacement contracts are native preparation behavior, not claims that the legacy Python-environment installer has the same filesystem layout.

Cancellation is exercised during a 30 MB extraction on a single-threaded asynchronous runtime. Extraction runs on an owned blocking task, so the cancellation timer remains responsive. A separate actual task abort waits until a native output file is observed, then drops the download owner. Its shared lock stays held until extraction stops and staging disappears; the next downloader acquires the lock only after cleanup. Failure leaves the previous runtime intact. Cache lookup removes owned post-promotion `.partial` and `.previous` directories while holding the exclusive lock.

The NVIDIA probe uses the released command and two-second deadline, with cached first-device results. Isolated real subprocesses cover success, process failure, invalid UTF-8 and an elapsed timeout. Their environment has no `uv` or interpreter on PATH, and every probe PID is gone before return. The native guard bounds output and uses a controlled unavailable result for malformed output; literal interpreter exception diagnostics are not reproduced.

Both real pinned runtimes were separately downloaded and installed through the production native method in a task-owned public asset store. The CPU and physical CUDA workers then loaded libraries from those installations. [Physical inference checks](../../../mluva-asr/tests/fixtures/README.md) independently verify required library/model contents before use, match sixteen actual released CPU/CUDA recognitions and observe owned NVIDIA compute contexts and process cleanup. Runtime readiness alone does not establish inference. These context-dependent tests are ignored by ordinary runs and were explicitly executed.

The ordinary workspace passes 112 native tests; formatting and Clippy with warnings denied pass. Eight context-dependent tests remain ignored by an ordinary workspace run, retaining their separately executed evidence. Fixture peers never ship. Installed app/widget remain v1.6.0. Parent speech/session ownership, broader model/language/fault acceptance, welcome/settings/controller integration, complete application workflows, distribution, final Python removal and same-host performance measurements remain required. The full Rust goal remains active.
